sources.note: Nothing on Ouma stress; Ouma figures only in Central Papuan sound-correspondence tables (pp. 190-205) and the source list ('Dutton 1976, 1980c, 1982, n.d.').

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1982. Borrowing in Austronesian and non-Austronesian languages of coastal south-east mainland Papua New Guinea. In A. Halim, L. Carrington & S.A. Wurm (eds), Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, vol. 1: Currents in Oceanic, 109-177. Pacific Linguistics C-74.
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix 3 'Ouma and Magori sound systems' (pp. 166-167, 'based on my own fieldwork') covers phoneme inventory, aspiration/frication of voiceless stops, status of glottal stop, [w]/[l]/[y] allophony, open syllables/no clusters; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom E. 1976. Austronesian languages: eastern part of south-eastern mainland Papua. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, 321-333. Pacific Linguistics C-39.

Dutton, Tom E. 1976. Magori and similar languages of South-East Papua. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 581-636. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.5.2.6.1 'Phonological evidence' (p. 594) gives only the segmental system for Ouma/Magori/Yoba/Bina (5 vowels; p t k glottal b d g m n v r, Ouma also h; allophony; 'All syllables are open and there are no consonant clusters'). Table 2 wordlists are in phonemic orthography with no stress marks.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1971. Languages of south-east Papua: a preliminary report. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics A-28 (read in the whole-volume scan, ANU hdl 1885/145019; the per-article PL-A28.1 files at sealang and ANU are mis-mapped to McElhanon's Selepet front matter).
sources.note: Ouma not mentioned (not yet 'discovered' in 1971); Magori noted as newly recognised Austronesian; no stress data.
